name: Create a terrain scene, save it and export the terrain
description: Generates a procedural terrain (subdivided grid displaced by noise), adds a material, sun light, sky and camera, saves the .blend project and exports only the terrain mesh (OBJ, GLB/GLTF, FBX or STL by file extension). Runs Blender headless through its Python API, so it needs no GUI and is fully verifiable.

parameters.name: blend_path
parameters.description: Where to save the .blend project (absolute path).

parameters.name: export_path
parameters.description: Where to export the terrain mesh; the extension (.obj, .glb, .gltf, .fbx, .stl) selects the format.

steps.title: Generate terrain, light, camera; save .blend; export terrain

args.code:
import bpy, os, mathutils
out_blend = r"{{blend_path}}"
out_export = r"{{export_path}}"
size = float("{{size}}")
subdiv = int("{{subdivisions}}")
strength = float("{{height}}")
seed = int("{{seed}}")

bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
scene = bpy.context.scene

bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_grid_add(x_subdivisions=subdiv, y_subdivisions=subdiv, size=size)
terrain = bpy.context.active_object
terrain.name = 'Terrain'

offset = bpy.data.objects.new('TerrainNoiseOffset', None)
scene.collection.objects.link(offset)
offset.location = ((seed * 137.13) % 1000.0, (seed * 71.7) % 1000.0, 0.0)

tex = bpy.data.textures.new('TerrainNoise', type='CLOUDS')
tex.noise_scale = max(size / 5.0, 0.5)
tex.noise_depth = 6
mod = terrain.modifiers.new('Displace', 'DISPLACE')
mod.texture = tex
mod.strength = strength
mod.texture_coords = 'OBJECT'
mod.texture_coords_object = offset
bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = terrain
bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=mod.name)
bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

mat = bpy.data.materials.new('TerrainMaterial')
mat.use_nodes = True
bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
if bsdf:
    bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value = (0.22, 0.38, 0.14, 1.0)
    bsdf.inputs['Roughness'].default_value = 0.9
terrain.data.materials.append(mat)

bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='SUN', location=(0, 0, size))
sun = bpy.context.active_object
sun.data.energy = 3.0
sun.rotation_euler = (0.7, 0.2, 0.6)

bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(size * 0.9, -size * 0.9, size * 0.55))
cam = bpy.context.active_object
cam.rotation_euler = (mathutils.Vector((0, 0, 0)) - cam.location).to_track_quat('-Z', 'Y').to_euler()
scene.camera = cam

world = scene.world or bpy.data.worlds.new('World')
scene.world = world
world.use_nodes = True
bg = world.node_tree.nodes.get('Background')
if bg:
    bg.inputs[0].default_value = (0.55, 0.72, 1.0, 1.0)

os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(out_blend)), exist_ok=True)
bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=out_blend)

bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='DESELECT')
terrain.select_set(True)
bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = terrain
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(out_export)), exist_ok=True)
ext = os.path.splitext(out_export)[1].lower()
if ext == '.obj':
    if hasattr(bpy.ops.wm, 'obj_export'):
        bpy.ops.wm.obj_export(filepath=out_export, export_selected_objects=True, export_materials=True)
    else:
        bpy.ops.export_scene.obj(filepath=out_export, use_selection=True)
elif ext in ('.glb', '.gltf'):
    bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=out_export, use_selection=True, export_format='GLB' if ext == '.glb' else 'GLTF_SEPARATE')
elif ext == '.fbx':
    bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(filepath=out_export, use_selection=True)
elif ext == '.stl':
    if hasattr(bpy.ops.wm, 'stl_export'):
        bpy.ops.wm.stl_export(filepath=out_export, export_selected_objects=True)
    else:
        bpy.ops.export_mesh.stl(filepath=out_export, use_selection=True)
else:
    raise ValueError('Unsupported export format: ' + ext)

print('TERRAIN_OK vertices=%d blender=%s' % (len(terrain.data.vertices), bpy.app.version_string))

hints.notes: If an operator is missing in this Blender version (e.g. exporters renamed in 4.x), check bpy.app.version and adapt the export call; the step output (stdout/stderr) shows the Python traceback.

failure_modes.symptom: glTF export fails with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'" (distribution-packaged Blender, e.g. Ubuntu's apt package)
failure_modes.recovery: Export to .obj, .fbx or .stl instead (no numpy needed), or install numpy for Blender's Python (installing software needs the user's approval). The official blender.org build bundles numpy.

failure_modes.symptom: app_script fails with 'Blender executable not found'
failure_modes.recovery: Locate Blender with app action find, or pass app_script.executable; ask the user to install it if absent (installing needs approval).

failure_modes.symptom: AttributeError: Calling operator 'bpy.ops.wm.obj_export' / 'export_scene.obj' could not be found
failure_modes.recovery: Exporter names differ by version. Use the other operator name, or export to .glb which is stable across versions.

notes: To view the result interactively: app launch Blender with params {"file": "<blend_path>"}.
For a richer environment, extend the script (scatter rocks/trees with particle systems or geometry nodes) and save it as a new workflow version.
